title: Python: D1 a class-body __call__ = None (or any class-scope rebinding of a method name) in a subclass must hide a base class def
description: Reported by the Opus review of #150 (not yet probed by the worker): methodLookup (calls.ts) never reads an MRO entry's class-scope bindings, so class B: def __call__(self); class C(B): __call__ = None; x = C(); x() gives an edge where Python raises TypeError. The same hole affects self.m(), Cls.m() and E1. Fix: an entry whose class scope binds the name by anything other than a def (assign, annotated, import, for, with) ends the lookup unresolved. Red then green fixtures per binding kind; mutation checks; per-site re-measure of the five pins.
implementationNotes: Built (DEC-303 (a31), D1). methodLookup now ends the lookup unresolved (receiver, needs-inference, the bin rebound defs already use) when an MRO class entry has no def of the name but its class scope binds it by anything that is not a def: bindsNameWithoutDef reads classInfo.scope.bindings for any binding whose kind is not def (assign, annotated with or without a value, tuple target, walrus, import, for, with, except-as, augmented, nested class). It applies to self.m(), Cls().m() (E1), x = Cls(); x.m() (6d), x() through __call__ (N3) and super() (which starts after the receiver class). A bare annotation-only 'name: T' is recorded by the walker as an assign with no value and so counts as a binding; Python does not bind it, so that case is conservative (refuses a lookup Python would resolve to the base); no corpus site exercises it as far as the per-site diff shows. Fixtures (test/python-calls.test.ts 'D1'): 11 binding kinds x 2 names (m, __call__) x the shapes (E1, 6d, self, N3 for __call__) refused; positive twins (unrelated binding, no binding, a binding of another name, a same-named def in C is C's own) still resolve; middle-class binding hides the base below it; super() stops at a binding and reaches the base past a non-binding; a sibling subclass and another name are unaffected. Mutation checks (source restored each time, 8 mutants): no guard 3 red, always-false 3, assign-only 1, import excluded 1, rebound excluded 1, nested class excluded 1, wrong bin 1; 'last binding only' survives and is equivalent on reachable states (when the guard runs methods has no def, so every binding is non-def). PER-SITE MEASURE, instrumented origin/dev abea54f vs the branch, five pins, multiset diff, entry counts equal on all five: ZERO inRepo edges changed. 45 sites changed in bin or reason: flask 17, jinja 15, httpx 3, rich 5, tqdm 5. 37 are receiver/instance-attribute to receiver/needs-inference (same bin, reason string only: flask 17, jinja 13, rich 2, tqdm 5); 8 are external/external-base to receiver/needs-inference (jinja compiler.py:1468 and nativetypes.py:73, httpx _models.py:1105,1106,1114, rich logging.py:99 and prompt.py:239,249), so resolvedExternal falls by 8 and receiverNeedsInference rises by 8 (jinja 2, httpx 3, rich 3). Those sites call a name the class body binds, previously credited to an external base. NOT MEASURED: precision of the 45 beyond the bin direction; I did not read each class body. GCLI-103 items not touched. Full gates: typecheck, lint, format:check, bun test 820 pass, lore check --strict 0.14.1.

ROUND 1 FIX (Opus BLOCK at 29c775e5 on one item; DEC-303 (a34) on the 8-site bin move stands, no code change). Fixture and record only. (1) 'except as' moved out of the hiding table: Python ends 'except E as NAME:' with an implicit del of NAME and the clause may never run, so after the try the class has no such attribute and C().m() reaches B.m; the walker records the as-target (addAsPatternBinding), so the guard refuses. That is conservative (an edge lost, none invented), now pinned in a separate fixture 'conservative: forms the walker counts as a class binding although Python does not keep one'. DISCLOSED CONSERVATIVE OVER-INCLUSIONS of the D1 guard, each loses an edge and none invents one, all pinned by that fixture except the first, which the earlier note already disclosed: annotation-only 'name: T' (recorded as an assign with no value); except-as; a comprehension target in a class body (the walker lands it in the class scope, Python 3 gives the comprehension its own); class-body 'global NAME' then 'NAME = ...' (stays a class binding in the walker); 'NAME = ...; del NAME' (del is not tracked). (2) Cls.m() fixture added: the 'cls' shape (C.m()) reaches methodLookup via the known-class path; the earlier note said Cls().m() for E1 and now the shapes are E1, 6d (x.m()), Cls.m(), self.m(), super() and N3 (x()). Positive twins cover the new shape. PRE-EXISTING WALKER GAPS FOUND BY THE REVIEW, wrong-edge direction (a binding is missed), NOT fixed here: PEP 695 'type m = ...' in a class body and 'with ctx() as (m, n)' tuple targets (probed on dev abea54f: each leaves C().m() with an edge to B.m, control 'm = None' gives none); filed as GCLI-107; match capture patterns are GCLI-101 (D2). Test gates: typecheck, lint, format:check, bun test, lore check --strict 0.14.1.
